key_drivers.name: OPEC August physical output shortfall
key_drivers.observed: Reuters survey data show OPEC-11 August crude output down 640,000 bpd month-on-month to 19.71 million bpd despite planned OPEC+ increases; Saudi export disruption and restricted Iranian shipments were major causes.
key_drivers.interpretation: Conflict is constraining realized supply independently of quota intent, reinforcing oil, freight and imported-inflation pressure.

key_drivers.name: Hormuz freight-fee partial relief
key_drivers.observed: Iran temporarily suspended a 10% freight-fee charge on foreign vessels carrying oil, gas and liquid petroleum products to or from Iran.
key_drivers.interpretation: Reduces one transport-cost friction but does not restore normal shipping or remove military risk.

key_drivers.name: Persistent Middle East oil/shipping shock
key_drivers.observed: Hormuz oil flows remain far below pre-war levels and Brent traded above $100.
key_drivers.interpretation: Imported-energy inflation, freight and insurance costs remain material headwinds for Taiwan margins and rate-sensitive equities.

key_drivers.name: OPEC 2026 demand downgrade
key_drivers.observed: OPEC cut 2026 world oil-demand-growth forecast to 380,000 bpd, its fifth consecutive downward revision.
key_drivers.interpretation: Adds demand-destruction/global-growth downside to the existing supply-driven energy shock.

geopolitical_global_risk.summary: The dominant Middle East maritime escalation remains unresolved. The new evidence is that August OPEC output fell materially despite intended OPEC+ increases, indicating conflict is constraining physical supply. Freight-fee relief is a partial operational adaptation, not normalization. OPEC's demand downgrade simultaneously points to growing demand-destruction/global-growth risk.

events.observed_evidence: Reuters survey data show OPEC-11 output fell 640,000 bpd month-on-month in August to 19.71 million bpd. Saudi export disruption and restricted Iranian shipments were cited as key causes despite planned OPEC+ increases.
events.semantic_interpretation: Realized supply is being constrained by conflict, strengthening energy-price and imported-inflation transmission into Taiwan while also raising demand-destruction risk.

events.observed_evidence: Iran temporarily suspended the 10% freight charge; Hormuz flows remained far below pre-war levels; Brent remained above $100; OPEC reduced 2026 oil-demand-growth forecast to 380,000 bpd.
events.semantic_interpretation: Partial cost relief does not offset persistent military/shipping risk. Taiwan remains exposed through imported energy, freight, inflation, yields and global-demand channels.

key_risks: Conflict-related supply losses may keep realized OPEC output below intended quota paths.
Further U.S.-Iran tanker or infrastructure attacks could reverse limited freight-cost relief immediately.
Sustained oil above $100 can reinforce global inflation and long-rate pressure.
OPEC's repeated demand downgrades signal increasing risk of demand destruction and weaker global manufacturing growth.
Taiwan energy-import, airline, petrochemical and high-duration technology exposures remain sensitive to oil, freight, FX and yield transmission.
